items.heading: Check the Marksheet Fact Together,
items.text: Check the marksheet fact together, before any exam conversation. Whether Mathematics genuinely appears as a Class 12 subject decides whether JEE-route engineering, architecture, and Maths-mandatory Economics Honours are open. Verify this first, not after a coaching fee is already paid.

items.heading: Separate "This Exam Requires Maths
items.text: Separate "this exam requires Maths eligibility" from "this exam has a quant section". These are two different problems with two different fixes. One is a hard eligibility wall; the other is a practice gap that consistent weekly work can close.

items.heading: Ask Which of the Fully
items.text: Ask which of the fully open doors already fits your child's real interest. Medicine and allied health, law through CLAT, most generalist government exams, and humanities-adjacent creative work are all completely open. Start the conversation there before dwelling on the blocked list.

items.heading: If a Bridge or Foundation
items.text: If a bridge or foundation Maths route is on the table, ask for the real weekly time commitment and the actual qualifier requirements. A bridge route like IIT Madras BS Data Science is genuine, but its qualifying exam is a real filter. Read the actual admissions page and a past qualifier paper together before committing money or a year of effort to it.

items.heading: "Without Maths, Half Your Career
items.text: "Without Maths, half your career options are gone", vague, and mostly wrong once you check the actual eligibility pages one by one.

items.heading: "Cat and Banking Exams Need
items.text: "CAT and banking exams need Maths, so forget them", they need a quantitative-aptitude score, not a 12th Maths subject on your marksheet.

items.heading: "Data Careers Are Only
items.text: "Data careers are only for Maths-stream students", true for the JEE-linked engineering route, false for several genuine bridge programmes.

items.heading: "Law, Humanities, and Government Jobs
items.text: "Law, humanities, and government jobs are only for students who couldn't do Maths", a status myth, not an eligibility fact.
